name: অগস্তীশ্বরর মন্দির, অগস্তিয়ম্পল্লি
deity: অগস্তীশ্বরর রূপে শিব, দেবী সৌন্দরনায়গী (ভাগম্প্রিয়া নায়গী)-র সঙ্গে
period: তেবারম যুগ (৭ম শতাব্দীতে গীত); পরবর্তী চোল কাঠামোগত মন্দির
summary: অগস্তিয়ম্পল্লি, সমুদ্রের কাছে বেদারণ্যমের কিছুটা দক্ষিণে, শিবকে অগস্তীশ্বরর রূপে দেবী সৌন্দরনায়গীর সঙ্গে সম্মান করে। তিরুজ্ঞান সম্বন্দর কর্তৃক গীত একটি পাডল পেট্র স্থলম্, মন্দিরটি ঋষি অগস্ত্যের সঙ্গে জড়িত, যিনি ঐতিহ্য অনুসারে এখানে শিবির স্থাপন করে শিবের বিবাহ দর্শন করেছিলেন এবং যাঁর অবস্থান থেকে গ্রামটি তার নাম নেয়।

sections.history: Agasthiyampalli lies a short distance south of Vedaranyam, on the way to Kodikkarai (Point Calimere), near the sea in Nagapattinam district. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar, and locally called Agasthiyar Kovil for its link to the sage Agastya. The stone temple is of the Chola period and later. (Sources differ on the exact distance from Vedaranyam, about 2–3 km.)
sections.architecture: A Dravidian coastal-delta temple, the shrine enshrines Agastheeswarar in the sanctum, with the goddess Soundaranayagi — also named Baagampriya Nayagi — in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas about the prakara. The walled courtyard and modest gopuram are typical of the Shiva temples of this low-lying southern tract near the coast.
sections.legends: The sage Agastya, by tradition, camped at this sivasthalam and was granted a vision of the wedding of Shiva and Parvati — the same marriage-darshan legend that binds the neighbouring Vedaranyam shrine — and the village of Agasthiyampalli takes its name from his stay. Shiva is worshipped here as Agastheeswarar, 'the lord of Agastya,' with Soundaranayagi beside him.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship, at the quiet scale of a coastal village shrine. Pilgrims on the Vedaranyam–Kodikkarai stretch of the Paadal Petra trail include Agasthiyampalli among their stops.
sections.experience: At Agasthiyampalli the pilgrim comes to a sea-edge shrine of the sage's lord. Before Agastheeswarar and Soundaranayagi, with the salt air of the lower delta near, the visitor finds the unhurried grace of a Tevaram temple of the Vedaranyam coast, and the memory of Agastya's vision of the divine wedding.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Agasthiyampalli lies about 2–3 km south of Vedaranyam, on the road toward Kodikkarai (Point Calimere), in Nagapattinam district. Vedaranyam is the nearest town, with buses and taxis to the village; Nagapattinam and Tiruvarur are the nearest rail heads.
